findings.title: Stripe subscription cancel runs inside the open DB transaction, risking inconsistent billing/data state and lock contention
findings.why: If the Stripe cancel succeeds but the subsequent commit fails, the subscription is cancelled while the account/org data remains; holding a multi-table transaction open across a slow external HTTP call also increases lock contention.
findings.fix: In packages/server/src/enterprise/services/account.service.ts delete(), move `await this.identityManager.cancelSubscription(organizaiton.subscriptionId)` to AFTER `await queryRunner.commitTransaction()` (alongside removeFolderFromStorage), so no external network call is made while the transaction is open; handle its failure with compensating logging rather than a rollback of already-committed data.
findings.evidence:
// Step 6: Cancel Stripe Subscription
+        await this.identityManager.cancelSubscription(organizaiton.subscriptionId)
+
+        await queryRunner.commitTransaction()
findings.verify_why: Diff confirms 'await this.identityManager.cancelSubscription(...)' executes before 'await queryRunner.commitTransaction()', so the external Stripe cancel runs inside the open multi-table transaction — a real partial-failure/consistency and lock-contention risk, not a style nit.

findings.title: Irreversible Stripe subscription cancellation runs inside the DB transaction before commit, so a commit failure leaves a cancelled subscription on an undeleted account
findings.why: cancelSubscription mutates external Stripe state that rollback cannot undo; if commitTransaction throws, the DB deletes roll back but the subscription is already cancelled, leaving billing and account state inconsistent.
findings.fix: In packages/server/src/enterprise/services/account.service.ts delete(), move the cancelSubscription call to after queryRunner.commitTransaction() (alongside removeFolderFromStorage), so the external/irreversible Stripe call only happens once the DB deletion is durably committed.
findings.evidence:
+        // Step 6: Cancel Stripe Subscription
+        await this.identityManager.cancelSubscription(organizaiton.subscriptionId)
+
+        await queryRunner.commitTransaction()
findings.verify_why: Diff literally shows `await this.identityManager.cancelSubscription(organizaiton.subscriptionId)` immediately before `await queryRunner.commitTransaction()` (Step 6); Stripe cancel is irreversible external state, so a commit failure rolls back the DB deletes/anonymization while the subscription stays cancelled — a genuine billing/account consistency bug, not style. Major (not critical) since it only triggers on the rare commit failure and affects the deleting user's own org.

findings.title: Stripe subscription is cancelled inside the open DB transaction, so a commit failure leaves billing cancelled but account undeleted
findings.why: The external Stripe call runs before commitTransaction(); if the commit then fails and the catch rolls back, the subscription is already cancelled while all user/workspace data is restored — inconsistent billing state, plus the network call holds DB locks.
findings.fix: In packages/server/src/enterprise/services/account.service.ts delete(), move the `this.identityManager.cancelSubscription(...)` call to AFTER `queryRunner.commitTransaction()` (alongside removeFolderFromStorage), or make cancellation idempotent/compensatable so a rollback can be reconciled.
